scope: TypeScript artifact planning for checked Operation actions with separate Query/Mapping value composition. Existing operation/action/profile contracts remain unchanged.
custody: Accept genuine checked composed actions from the exact compiled graph, boundary and field model. Bind this exact contract and the existing reconciled source capsule. Reject forged snapshots, unknown selection fields, unsafe paths and artifact collisions.
dependencies: Derive named Query, Mapping, public Interface, Rule and Event generator roots from each action. Select factory bindings explicitly under the existing exact field closure. Reuse existing profile generators; never replace named contracts with generic execution or identity lookup.
absence: Each require-present Query binding has one explicit caller-selected failure code; no code is inferred. Preserve optional results when preserve is selected and retain QUERY_CARDINALITY for multiple matches.
runtime: Emit transaction-scoped collection reads and named value calls before guards and effects. Preserve single preparation, validation-before-filtering, rollback/cleanup visibility, state-and-outbox atomic intent, awaited settlement, and no automatic retry after commit uncertainty.
artifacts: Generate explicit relative imports from planned modules. Bind exact dependency contracts and artifacts in a compact Operation descriptor, without embedding the compiled graph or a runtime expression interpreter. Deduplicate identical artifact bytes and reject conflicting paths. Batch order does not change an individual Operation module.
effects: Planning returns immutable artifacts only. It does not write files, execute providers, deliver Events, admit definitions, publish a package or establish production durability.
completion_boundary: This candidate planner requires separate public compiler/CLI integration, source-capsule selection, full native target coverage and whole-application verification before release completeness may be claimed.
